text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

Australian explorer JOHN MACKAY, who became a sea captain after the Government failed to reward his efforts in locating the Mackay pastoral district in Queensland and his surveying of Port Mackay, was born in 1839.
Australian boundary rider and poet BARCROFT BOAKE, who wrote "Where The Dead Men Lie" and hanged himself with his stockwhip at the age of 26, was born in 1866.
American 'jazz' singer AL JOLSON was born in 1886.
Russian/Australian pioneer music publisher and broadcaster MICHEL (FRANK) ALBERT, who built the classic Sydney mansion 'Boomerang' at Potts Point, was born in 1874.
Australian actor CHIPS RAFFERTY (JOHN GOFFAGE), one of the best-loved actors of early Aussie movies, was born in 1909.
American playwright TENNESSEE WILLIAMS was born in 1914.
American actor LEONARD NIMOY, known as 'Doctor Spock' in the Star Trek series, was born in 1931.
American actor JAMES CAAN was born in 1939.

American singer DIANA ROSS was born on this day in 1944. The lead singer with the 'Supremes' had several hits with the group such as "Baby Love" (1964), "Stop In The Name Of Love" (1965), "You Can't Hurry Love" (1965) and " Happening" (1967). The last hit before the group split up was "Someday We'll Be Together Again" (1969). Her solo hits included "Ain't No Mountain High Enough" (1970), "Do You Know Where You're Going To" (1975), "Upside Down" (1980) and "Chain Reaction" (1986). There were countless top ten hits, some were duets with artists such as MARVIN GAYE, MICHALE JACKSON, SMOKEY ROBINSON, STEVIE WONDER, and the combination with LIONEL RITCHIE, that produced "Endless Love". It was at number one in the US for nine consecutive weeks in 1981.
British/Australian singer/actor JON ENGLISH was born in 1949.
** EVENTS **
1780 : The British Gazette and Sunday Monitor, the first
Sunday newspaper in Britain, was published.
1827 : German composer LUDIWG VAN BEETHOVEN died at the
age of 57.
1839 : The first Henley-on-Thames rowing regatta was
staged.
1871 : The Paris Commune, an insurrection of Paris
against the French government, was formally set up.
1878 : The world's first Game Reserve was designated -
the SABI GAME RESERVE in South Africa.
1892 : American poet WALT WHITMAN died. He became a
revolutionary figure in American literature after the publication of his "Leaves of Grass".
1902 : The man who at one stage controlled 90 per cent of
the world's diamond production, British imperialist CECIL JOHN RHODES, died in Cape Town at the age of 48.
1919 : Australian explorer/prospector ERNEST HENRY, who
founded the Great Australian Copper Mine on Cloncurry in Queensland, died in Sydney at the age of 82.
1923 : French actress SARAH BERNHARDT, who had one of her
legs amputated and returned to the stage performing with a wooden leg, died at the age of 78. She had been loved by millions, and had made several world tours in the 1870's.
1934 : The Queensland Flying Doctor service announced it
would extend into Western Australia. The service was started in 1928 by the Australian Inland Mission of the Presbyterian Church. Its first flight was to Julia Creek in Central Queensland.
1936 : New Zealand radio began the first live broadcasts
from the nation's Parliament.
1942 : The Nazis began sending Jews to the Auschwitz
concentration camp in Poland.
1945 : In World War Two, the Battle of Iwo Jima ended.
During the battle about 22,000 Japanese troops were killed or captured and more than 4,500 U.S. troops were killed.
1945 : DAVID LLOYD GEORGE, British statesman and Liberal
prime minister, died; he also negotiated Irish independence in 1921.
1958 : In London, Britain's first parking tickets were
issued to motorists.
1959 : RAYMOND CHANDLER, U.S. crime writer, died. Creator
of the private detective character Philip Marlowe in his novels including, "The Big Sleep" and "Farewell My Lovely".
1964 : BARBARA STREISAND triumphed on Broadway with the
new musicial comedy "Funny Girl".
1973 : British dramatist, composer and actor NOEL COWARD
died.
1973 : The first women stockbroker set foot in the London
Stock Exchange.
1979 : Israeli Prime Minister MENACHEM BEGIN and Egyptian
President ANWAR SADAT signed an historic peace treaty, in the presence of American President JIMMY CARTER.
1980 : A former Air Force Corporal claimed that about 100

servicemen came into contact with contaminated aircraft at Maralinga during the 1953-54 atomic tests. It was also claimed that several Aborigines died after a "rolling black mist" covered their camp after a 1953 atomic test in South Australia. Aborigines about 170 km north of the Emu Field test site said many went blind, permanently, others developed rashes and others developed vomiting and diarrhoea attacks when the mist rolled in.
1982 : The world's first test-tube twins were born in
Cambridge.
1983 : The so-called "Fourth Man" of Britain's
upper-class spy ring, ANTHONY BLUNT, died of a heart attack. BLUNT had recruited KIM PHILBY, DONALD MACLEAN and GUY BURGESS to spy for the Soviet Union.
1984 : The 100-dollar note was introduced in Australia.
1985 : The first son of the PRINCE and PRINCESS OF WALES,
PRINCE WILLIAM, shook hands for the first time in public. In training for the throne, WILLIAM shook the hand of the pilot who flew him and his family from Aberdeen to London.
1992 : PRINCE ANDREW and the DUCHESS OF YORK, SARAH
FERGUSON, officially separated.
1992 : Former world heavyweight boxing champion MIKE
TYSON was sentenced to six years in prison for rape.
1996 : Former U.S. Secretary of State EDMUND MUSKIE died
after a heart attack.
